speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A physics reading programme
summary: The opening question is \ru{Что надо знать из физики?}; an uncertain marginal attribution says ``following Sinai?''. The programme lists classical and Hamiltonian mechanics; quantum mechanics and scattering; relativity and field theory; and quantum field theory, including second quantization, Bose and Fermi statistics, functional integrals, perturbation series, Feynman diagrams, renormalization and Yang--Mills fields. Arnold, Landau--Lifshitz, Fermi, Weinberg and Hepp are reading suggestions. Consultation with physicists and a typed version are requested. No theorem, calculation or definite research problem is stated, so the programme is preserved without manufacturing mathematical occurrences. Gindikin begins on the same page; the catalogue's P000659--P000660 window overlaps that next record.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin, with I. M. Gelfand
title: SL(2, R), integral geometry and analytic separation of series
summary: The group is represented as the determinant-one quadric, and the regular representation is studied through hyperplane and line integrals. Gelfand distinguishes separation into series from decomposition into individual irreducibles. The announced real-transform kernels isolate discrete and continuous parts; two complex domains then realize the positive and negative discrete parts as Hardy boundary values. The lecture ends with an explicit kernel and Arnold's conjecture identifying the domains by their fractional-linear action. The exact subsequent paper is \citet{gelfandgindikin1977complex}, received 6 June 1977. Its kernel has an additional nonconstant factor absent from the notebook. P000661--P000662 unmistakably continue this lecture, despite the catalogue's narrower page window.

speaker: Academic-year heading
summary: This catalogue entry labels the academic year and overlaps the opening lectures. It supplies no separately identifiable mathematical exposition. The actual occurrences in its page window belong to records 397--398 and 400--403 and are indexed there once.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Superalgebras, supergroups and supermanifolds: announced heading
summary: Immediately below the date 13/IX-76, the manuscript gives Kirillov's name and this title, then explicitly switches to Fuchs and the Weil algebra. No intervening exposition is recorded. The title is retained as a programme heading; Fuchs's formulas and Kirillov's later intervention are assigned to records 401 and 402. The broad catalogue window P000662--P000664 must not be read as an independent three-page Kirillov lecture.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: The Weil algebra and its differential
summary: Fuchs constructs the graded algebra \(\Lambda\mathfrak g^*\otimes S\mathfrak g^*\), specifies its differential on generators, explains the signed Leibniz rule and gives the structure-constant formula on the symmetric generators. The concluding acyclicity statement omits the surviving degree-zero constants. Characteristic classes are announced for a future meeting, not developed here. This is established Weil--Cartan theory: \citet{cartan1950weil,cartan1950transgression}. The lecture begins on P000663 and ends before the explicit Kirillov intervention on P000664.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Transgression and invariant forms on compact Lie groups
summary: A short intervention explains the purpose of the Weil algebra in computing compact Lie-group cohomology. The intended correspondence is between primitive odd cohomology generators and indecomposable symmetric invariant polynomials. The notebook states a stronger, false dimension equality for all invariant forms and reverses the differential direction in its transgression shorthand. The surrounding Fuchs and Arnold lectures belong to separate records.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Point equivalence of second-order equations and projective geometry
summary: Arnold explicitly revisits nineteenth-century work of Lie, Tresse and Liouville and Cartan's 1924 projective connections. The lecture separates point linearization, pairs of line fields in a contact three-manifold, projective parameters along solutions, and inequivalent projective structures on a circle. It then normalizes the quadratic transverse terms, obtains a relative 5/2-density, and constructs projective scalar invariants from its reciprocal power. A damaged global question and Gelfand's proposed cohomological connection are recorded without inventing missing quantifiers. The local normalization calculations can be checked, but the stated flatness implication needs additional hypotheses.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Lie superalgebras and the Wess--Zumino multiplet
summary: Novikov explicitly recommends Ogievetsky's UFN review and a Zumino review, with Volkov and Akulov noted in the margin. He defines Lie superalgebras, uses real Majorana spinors to construct supertranslations, and records Gelfand's request to adjoin Lorentz generators. The Wess--Zumino chiral multiplet, its auxiliary fields, Lagrangian and infinitesimal transformations occupy the remainder. The material predates the talk, as the cited 1975 review confirms. Several faithful notebook errors require emendation: Gol'fand's name, the scalar label on the spinor, an uncontracted kinetic index, and incompatible coefficients between the two action formulas.

speaker: A. A. Migdal
title: Why quarks suggest local colour gauge fields
summary: Migdal's short discussion begins after Novikov's variations on P000669. It moves from three-quark nucleons and quark--antiquark mesons to short-distance freedom, confinement, relativistic locality and the colour/flavour matrix. No QCD field equation is actually written. Its force-law and uncertainty-principle slogans are not mathematical confinement proofs. The matrix uses three light flavours and three colours; it should not be interpreted as nine independent flavours or as an exhaustive 1976 particle inventory. Bernstein's dated 18/X-76 lecture starts only on P000670 and is outside this record.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Superdomains, Berezin integration, and Stokes boundaries
summary: The dated continuation begins on P000670, after a separate question about factors. Bernstein explains superfunctions, parity-preserving morphisms, nilpotent Taylor expansion, and why a boundary requires an embedded subsupermanifold in addition to its ordinary body. The circle and half-line examples lead to the Stokes problem, soon printed by Bernstein and Leites. P000673--P000674 explicitly form a retrospective summary of earlier super talks copied from I.~Dorfman's notebook; their definitions and linear algebra are indexed here with that provenance, rather than assigned a new seminar date. The catalogue's P000668--P000675 span also includes adjoining talks.

speaker: V. N. Popov [catalogue; attribution conflict]
title: Connections, free Yang--Mills fields, and Ricci-flat metrics
summary: The notes begin on P000675 with Gelfand's request for an elementary explanation of a connection and a reference to Yang and Mills. They develop gauge covariance, the principal-bundle equation \(H\delta_h\Phi=0\), its independence of the auxiliary vertical metric, and the affine-frame realization of the vacuum Einstein equations. The last two results match D.~A.~Popov's 1975 paper and D.~A.~Popov--L.~I.~Daikhin's 1975 note exactly. The supplied catalogue calls the speaker V.~N.~Popov, while the handwritten heading gives only Popov; that conflict is retained explicitly. Mathematical identification of the papers does not prove a correction of the speaker's initials. The identified notes occupy P000675--P000677, narrower than the catalogue's P000673--P000679 packet.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Euler products, compact-group heat kernels, and affine Lie algebras
summary: Bernstein explains Euler and Jacobi identities, Macdonald's root-system generalization, and Kostant's expression through characters and the Casimir. A shifted spectral zeta function is introduced, but its displayed reflection equation lacks the necessary Mellin completion. Olshanetsky intervenes on radial Laplacians and quantum integrability. Bernstein then gives the Cartan-matrix construction and the affine \(A_2\) loop-algebra example. The date 22 November is supplied by the catalogue; the corresponding handwritten start on P000678 is undated and P000680 ends with a New Year greeting. This evidence does not establish additional sessions within the packet. The mathematical notes are P000678--P000680, rather than the catalogue's wider P000677--P000681 span.

title: YEAR 1977
summary: This catalogue record is the archival year heading between the late-1976 material and the dated Manin notes beginning on P000681. It supplies no independent mathematical statement. The wider catalogue packet P000679--P000681 contains the neighboring talks; no content is invented for the heading.

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Spectral curves, rank-two solitons, and filtered bimodules
summary: Manin begins with a reference to Calogero's boomeron, then describes a fourth-order Lax system and an explicitly singular, periodically oscillating rank-two pulse. The algebraic part passes from commuting operators to a spectral curve and eigenfunction bundles, contrasts rank-one Jacobian motion with higher-rank bundle moduli, and gives the filtered-bimodule construction and its inverse. Two further connections yield evolution and zero-curvature equations. The material has an unusually close later match in Manin's 1978 survey, including a sign error in the flatness formula that survives into the printed English translation. The last sentence announces Duistermaat for the next meeting; it does not contain that lecture.

speaker: J. J. Duistermaat
title: Morse indices, Lagrangian intersections, and the spherical trace formula
summary: The first part explains the finite Morse index of a regular variational problem with general endpoint constraints through a path of Lagrangian subspaces. The general-boundary theory was publicly presented in May 1974. The second part passes from spherical convolution to a distributional Selberg formula and joint spectral asymptotics; its identifiable continuation is the 1979 paper with Kolk and Varadarajan. The notebook suppresses transversality and normalization conventions, indexes orbital terms by elements rather than conjugacy classes, and ends with a remainder exponent not supported by the matched theorem. These are assessed separately.

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Filtered bimodules, nodal spectral curves, and soliton equations
summary: This continuation recapitulates the bimodule reconstruction of commuting operators, Lax evolutions, and zero-curvature equations, then constructs the modules explicitly on an affine line with pairs of points identified. The block interpolation matrix, filtration, connection matrices, and operator orders closely match Chapter III, sections 2 and 5, of Manin's 1978 Russian exposition (English translation 1979). Several signs and indices in the notebook are demonstrably inconsistent with that construction. The final question about the behaviour of an \(N\)-soliton solution specifies neither an equation nor a limiting regime; it is retained without manufacturing a new open problem.

speaker: A. M. Gabrielov
title: Pontryagin cycles, changes of sections, and hypersimplicial chains
summary: Gelfand motivates a combinatorial theory by local Euler-characteristic formulas and the difficulty of noncommuting rotations. Gabrielov then describes the first Pontryagin class by a corank-two degeneracy locus, reduces the chain calculations to pairs of sections of a real plane bundle, and organizes their cobordisms by hypersimplices. The notes identify MacPherson's February 1977 Bourbaki exposition, which was published in the 1978 proceedings. The core constructions were already in the two Gabrielov--Gelfand--Losik papers of 1975. The final diagrams sketch low-dimensional chain assignments rather than a new, fully specified open problem.

speaker: M. I. Graev
title: Range equations, differential-form inversion, and complexes of lines
summary: Graev develops the complex line transform in three-space, its range equations, and inversion by integrating a closed \((1,1)\)-form over a cycle of directions. This matches the explicitly cited 1967 Gelfand--Graev--Shapiro paper. The classification of admissible complexes matches the 1968 Gelfand--Graev paper, including its algebraic and genericity conditions. The final discussion of linear complexes is a separate projective-geometric construction: nondegenerate and special complexes must be distinguished, and it is not automatically an example of the preceding admissibility theorem.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Poncelet closure and Figiel’s short proof of Dvoretzky’s theorem
summary: The short intervention above Vershik's heading states the Poncelet porism for two conics, asks for the closing condition, and points to Griffiths's 1976 paper. It then identifies Figiel's 1976 Compositio proof of Dvoretzky's theorem. This material precedes record 415 on the manuscript page despite the catalogue record-number order.

speaker: A. M. Vershik
title: Probability, the Young graph, and Plancherel asymptotics
summary: The manuscript starts Vershik's talk below Gelfand's intervention on the page headed 28 March 1977, without another date. The catalogue's 4 April date is therefore corrected here, with the catalogue value preserved in the provenance. The exposition moves from Young's finite representation theory and branching paths to Plancherel growth, the limit shape, Ulam's longest increasing subsequence problem, and a proposed fluctuation theorem. The exact limit-shape and first-row results are in the 1977 Vershik--Kerov announcement, received in December 1976. The fluctuation line is not an exact statement of the later Kerov theorem: both the displayed fourth-root scaling and the white-noise description require correction.

speaker: A. Tyurin
title: Packets of flat representations and exponential and Schwarzian periods
summary: The scan identifies only A. Tyurin; the catalogue gives A. S., whereas the exactly matching 1977 paper and 1978 survey are by A. N. Tyurin. This identification is made from the publications, not from an expanded manuscript initial. The talk compares flat representations having isomorphic underlying holomorphic bundles, explicitly solves the rank-one packet problem by logarithmic differentials, and turns to Schwarzian derivatives and projective monodromy. The GL(n) packet dimension in the notes is the fixed-determinant dimension, and the universal assertion about any two irreducible representations is false, already for unitary characters. Both require mathematical annotations rather than silent transcription repairs.

title: Catalogue heading for 1977–78 and adjacent next-year context
summary: This catalogue record marks the 1977--78 academic-year boundary; it is retained as a heading, with no fabricated 1976--77 mathematical occurrences. On P000705 the source starts the seminar's thirty-fourth year and proposes noncommutative algebraic geometry in connection with Bernstein, I.~M.~Gelfand and S.~I.~Gelfand. A distinct heading then names V.~Drinfeld and Atiyah's work on Yang--Mills equations. P000705--P000706 contain the beginning of that adjacent talk: self-dual curvature on \(S^4\), conformal invariance of the Hodge star on two-forms, a heuristic quantization/determinant discussion, the twistor map \(\mathbb{CP}^3\to\mathbb{HP}^1=S^4\) with fibers \(\mathbb{CP}^1\), and a correspondence with bundles trivial on twistor fibers, followed by the quaternionic real structure. These adjacent contents are inventoried for coverage and must be catalogued with the next academic year. The visible date is transcribed as 5/IV-77, in tension with the boundary; the exact month is left unresolved rather than silently changed to September.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Exterior-algebra modules and algebraic bundles (manuscript: 13 February 1978)
summary:
\textbf{Provenance correction.} The supplied catalogue date, 13 February 1977, is corrected in the structured \texttt{date} field to the manuscript date, 13 February 1978; the catalogue value is preserved here and in the provenance ledger. The scan of P000753 unambiguously reads \ru{13/II--78 г.}; P000757 begins a new lecture, \ru{27/II--78 г.}. Thus this is a 1977--78 talk accidentally included in the requested package, not evidence for a 1976--77 announcement. The occurrence prefix \texttt{1977-437} follows the format rule that YEAR is the first year of the actual academic year. The requested record is retained in this package as an explicitly identified chronological appendix. P000752 is an adjacent physics tail; P000757--P000758 belong to the next, separately dated, S.~I.~Gelfand lecture. They are accounted for in the source ledger and corrections, without assigning their new content to record~437.

The talk explains how finite graded modules over an exterior algebra produce complexes on projective space. A fibrewise exactness condition singles out vector bundles; graded free summands disappear, and every bundle is represented uniquely up to stable module isomorphism. Twisting is expressed through a cosyzygy and a grading shift, followed by an outline of the inverse construction from large-twist sections. I.~M.~Gelfand calls for coherent sheaves and derived categories, and Serre's projective module--sheaf correspondence closes the surviving lecture. The exact publication is \citet[Theorem~1 and its remarks]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}: received 10 January 1978, before the manuscript's lecture date, published in the 1978 Russian volume; the English translation bears a 1979 copyright imprint. A submission date is not, by itself, a verified date of public circulation. Class A here denotes subsequent publication of the current work; it does not assert discovery after the lecture. The modern derived equivalence is given there by Theorem~2, but is not silently attributed to the surviving lecture as a fully stated theorem.
